questions.stem: What is the difference between magnification and resolution?

options.text: Resolution is always higher than magnification
Magnification is about clarity; resolution is about size
Magnification is how much larger an image appears; resolution is the ability to distinguish between two close points

questions.explanation: Magnification is how many times larger an image appears compared to the actual object. Resolution is the ability to distinguish between two separate points that are close together.

questions.stem: Which type of microscope has the highest resolution?
questions.explanation: Electron microscopes have the highest resolution (around 0.1 nm) because they use a beam of electrons instead of light, which has a much shorter wavelength.

questions.stem: What is the maximum useful magnification of a light microscope?
questions.explanation: Light microscopes have a maximum useful magnification of about x1,500. Beyond this, the image becomes blurry because the resolution limit has been reached.

questions.stem: How do you calculate total magnification using a compound light microscope?

options.text: Add the eyepiece and objective lens magnifications
Subtract the objective from the eyepiece magnification
Divide the eyepiece by the objective lens magnification
Multiply the eyepiece lens magnification by the objective lens magnification

questions.explanation: Total magnification = eyepiece lens magnification x objective lens magnification. For example, x10 eyepiece x x40 objective = x400 total magnification.

questions.stem: Which type of electron microscope produces 3D images of surfaces?
questions.explanation: The scanning electron microscope (SEM) scans the surface of a specimen with electrons and produces detailed 3D images of the surface structure.

questions.stem: Why can electron microscopes not be used to view living specimens?

options.text: Specimens must be placed in a vacuum and prepared with heavy metals

questions.explanation: Electron microscopes require specimens to be placed in a vacuum and treated with heavy metal stains, which kills living cells. Only light microscopes can view living specimens.

options.text: A photograph taken through a microscope

questions.explanation: A micrograph is a photograph or digital image taken through a microscope. An electron micrograph is taken using an electron microscope, while a light micrograph uses a light microscope.
